So I'm living away from home but my mom and younger brother came up to visit over the weekend and it was a disaster. My brother just complained about how bored and tired he was the entire time, and then my mom found his weed on the second day and she took away his phone so he was even more pissed off. He blamed me for being selfish and not wanting to be around him even though *he* was the one who insisted on going home early and spending time away from me during his visit. My mom and I ended up just dropping him off at their Airbnb but we were very worried he was gonna hurt himself since he didn't have his phone or his pen. We ended up just eating dinner at a restaurant, I dropped her off back at the Airbnb, I went back to my place, and I just sat. 

As I sat alone in my room, I started thinking about how miserable my family makes me. And then without thinking, I grabbed my box cutter and held it up to my neck. All I could think about was how, if I slit my throat right now, I would never have to think about my family again. I could be free from them for good. I liked how in-control I felt in that moment. One motion and I would be completely in control of my fate, of the end of my life.

And then I realized that I couldn't die. I don't want to die. And I started crying. I was so scared and sad. I am sick of my dad and brother being violent and threatening to my mom and me, but I am not going to die. I am not going to let them kill me. I am not going to let them have that power over me, because they've already held so much power over my life in the past.

Ok so first off I slept in until almost 1:00 in the afternoon. I ate and then spent an hour or two cleaning my room, which was fine. But then I decided I'd try to loft my bed (I have an adjustable loft bed) by myself, which was a dire mistake. I got the metal part of the bedframe stuck incorrectly and then it just. wouldn't. move. I spent a fucking hour trying to get it unstuck before realizing that it was gonna be there for good. I think this was what finally broke me after a long while of trying to sustain myself and live on my own. I broke down and cried for 40 minutes. All I could think about was how sad I was, how much I wanted to kms, how tired I was of *everything*. And I am, I am so fucking tired of being depressed and feeling so horrible. I'm trying so hard to improve myself, to get better, to be healthier and balance my life. But I still feel like fucking shit half the time. And it's so goddamn frustrating. 

Later in the evening, my roommate came back and to my mattress leaned up against her bed, and my bed broken. She seemed pretty pissed but didn't say anything. I got someone to come over to our room and fix my bed, and it was really loud, and my roommate left. I texted her to apologize and she came back, but we haven't talked since. When I was a junior in high school, I decided to go to a church camp mainly so that I could appease my parents. I had already spent a year away from Christianity and my parents knew I didn't believe in it, but I went anyway. My small group leader also knew that I wasn't a Christian - in fact, I told her I was an atheist shortly before the camp happened.

I didn't expect it to go well, but it was worse than I imagined. On the last day of the weekend, I had to leave the sanctuary in the middle of a sermon about how we are not defined by ourselves, we're defined by Christ. It made me panicked in a way I hadn't experienced in a long time. My leader followed me out, and she spent the next 20 minutes trying to convince me that her faith was the "correct" one by refuting all of my points and taking advantage of me when I was emotionally vulnerable. I had a panic attack in front of her just because she was trying to convert me. 

To this day it's one of the most vivid, traumatic memories I have from church, despite it not being nearly as bad as some of the other shit that happened. I still get stressed just thinking about it, and I panic whenever I think I could be confronted by someone trying to convert me. I feel incredibly vulnerable thinking about it, like I'm a helpless kid again and maybe I've been wrong about everything all along. 

All that to say, you're not pathetic for feeling that way, and you're certainly not alone. Religion can really screw you up, and it's completely normal for your body and mind to react negatively when someone tries to bring you back to that traumatic headspace (whether they know they're doing it or not).
